es.summary: Prueba no invasiva de bienestar fetal que registra la FCF en relación con los movimientos del feto, sin provocar contracciones. Un NST reactivo es tranquilizador.
key_points: Se puede realizar desde las 28 semanas de gestación.
Reactivo: 2 o más aceleraciones de al menos 15 lpm durante 15 segundos en 20 minutos (desde las 32 semanas).
Antes de las 32 semanas basta con aceleraciones de 10 lpm durante 10 segundos.
No reactivo: aceleraciones insuficientes en 20 a 40 minutos; no siempre significa un problema (el feto puede estar dormido).
Si sigue no reactivo a los 40 minutos, se avisa y se suele pedir un perfil biofísico.

purpose: Valorar el bienestar fetal en embarazos con riesgo: movimientos fetales disminuidos, embarazo pasado de la FPP, HTA, diabetes, embarazo múltiple o complicaciones previas.
Es una prueba sin estrés para el feto: no se provocan contracciones.
procedure: Colocar a la embarazada semisentada o en decúbito lateral.
Colocar dos transductores: uno para la FCF y otro (tocodinamómetro) para la actividad uterina.
Pedirle que presione el botón cada vez que sienta moverse al bebé.
Registrar por 20 minutos; extender hasta 40 minutos si no hay aceleraciones.
safety: Si el feto no se mueve, puede estar dormido: ofrecer un refrigerio o bebida azucarada.
Avisar si aparecen desaceleraciones o si el resultado es no reactivo a los 40 minutos.
nursing_care: Explicar el motivo de la prueba y qué va a pasar.
Evitar el decúbito supino prolongado (hipotensión supina).
Informar el resultado al médico y dar la educación indicada.
documentation: Anotar EG, duración, línea de base de la FCF, aceleraciones, desaceleraciones, movimientos fetales y resultado (reactivo o no reactivo).

en.summary: A noninvasive test for fetal well-being that records the fetal heart rate in relation to fetal movement, without causing contractions. A reactive NST is reassuring.
key_points: A nonstress test can be performed starting at 28 weeks' gestation.
Reactive: the FHR increases by at least 15 bpm above the baseline for 15 seconds, two or more times during a 20-minute period (32 weeks or greater).
Before 32 weeks, accelerations of 10 bpm for 10 seconds are enough.
Nonreactive: not enough accelerations within the 20- to 40-minute window; it does not necessarily indicate a health problem (the fetus may be sleeping).
After 40 minutes, if the test remains nonreactive, the nurse notifies the provider and further testing, often a BPP, is planned.

purpose: Assess fetal well-being in at-risk pregnancies: decreased fetal movement, past the due date, high blood pressure, diabetes, multiples or previous complications.
This test places no stress on the fetus: no contractions are induced.
procedure: Position the pregnant person semi-reclined or side-lying.
The nurse will attach two devices: one measures the fetal heart rate, and the other records uterine activity.
The pregnant person presses a button each time they feel the fetus move.
Record for 20 minutes; extend to 40 minutes if there are no accelerations.
safety: If the fetus isn't moving, it may be sleeping: offer a snack or sugary drink to wake the fetus.
Notify the provider if decelerations appear or the test is nonreactive at 40 minutes.
nursing_care: Explain why the test is recommended and what happens during the test.
Avoid lying flat on the back for a long time (supine hypotension).
Report the result to the provider and give the prescribed teaching.
documentation: Record GA, length of the test, FHR baseline, accelerations, decelerations, fetal movements and the result (reactive or nonreactive).

summary.0.quote: A nonstress test (NST) is a noninvasive test for fetal well-being that provides a graphic of the fetal heart pattern in relation to the movement of the fetus ( Figure 13.10 ).

summary.1.quote: If the fetal heart rate increases by at least 15 bpm above the baseline for 15 seconds for a fetus at 32 weeks or greater, or 10 bpm for 10 seconds in the fetus less than 32 weeks, two or more times during a 20-minute testing period, it is considered a reactive NST and is a reassuring result.

key_points.0.quote: A nonstress test can be performed starting at 28 weeks’ gestation (U.S. National Library of Medicine, 2021a).

key_points.1.quote: If the fetal heart rate increases by at least 15 bpm above the baseline for 15 seconds for a fetus at 32 weeks or greater, or 10 bpm for 10 seconds in the fetus less than 32 weeks, two or more times during a 20-minute testing period, it is considered a reactive NST and is a reassuring result.

key_points.2.quote: Before 32 weeks, accelerations of the FHR are expected to peak at 10 bpm above the baseline with a duration of at least 10 seconds but less than 2 minutes.

key_points.4.quote: After 40 minutes, if the test remains nonreactive, the nurse will notify the health-care provider and a plan for further testing, often a BPP, is relayed to the pregnant person by the nurse.

sections.purpose.1.quote: This test places no stress on the fetus.

sections.procedure.0.quote: The pregnant person will lie on a reclining chair or an exam table when the test is performed in the office or clinic.

sections.procedure.1.quote: The nurse will attach two devices around the pregnant person’s abdomen. One will measure the fetal heart rate, and the other will record the pregnant person’s uterine activity.

sections.procedure.2.quote: The pregnant person will be instructed to press a button on a cable attached to the fetal monitor each time they feel the fetus move.
